[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The VPC-backed OpenSearch domain requires the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch service-linked role to exist before creation, but it has no dependency on the conditionally managed role. Add an explicit depends_on so the domain is not created before the service-linked role.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The OpenSearch domain uses VPC options, which require the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch service-linked role to exist first. The AWS provider documentation explicitly recommends a depends_on for this same-time creation case, but the domain has no dependency on the configured service-linked-role resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The VPC-enabled OpenSearch domain `:resource.aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch` should wait for `:resource.aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch`. The AWS provider documentation states that the service-linked role must exist before creating a domain with VPC options; the domain currently has no dependency on that role.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch uses vpc_options (subnets + security groups) but has no dependency on aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch. Per AWS provider docs, the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch service-linked role must exist before a VPC domain can be created; when both are created together a depends_on from the domain to the role is required to order creation. Add an explicit depends_on.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
The VPC-based OpenSearch domain `:resource.aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch` uses vpc_options, which requires the AWS service-linked role for OpenSearch (`:resource.aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch`) to already exist. Per the provider docs, the domain must be ordered after the `aws_iam_service_linked_role` (typically via `depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch]`). No attribute reference or depends_on expresses this today, so on a fresh apply the domain can fail with "service-linked role not found".

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The VPC-based OpenSearch domain requires the AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService service-linked role to already exist, otherwise the first `terraform apply` fails with "You must create the service-linked role for Amazon ES". The example defines `aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch` (gated by `var.create_iam_service_linked_role`) precisely for this, but `aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch` never references it and has no `depends_on`, so nothing orders the role before the domain. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch]` on the domain.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The OpenSearch domain `:resource.aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch` is provisioned into a VPC (`vpc_options`, via `:module.aws_vpc`), and the AWS service-linked role (`:resource.aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch`, gated on `var.create_iam_service_linked_role`) is created in the same configuration. The `aws_elasticsearch_domain` documentation explicitly states that VPC-based domains require the `AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService` service-linked role to exist before domain creation, and that `depends_on` must be used when the role is created alongside the domain. Without this ordering, first-time `apply` can fail with the domain returning an access-denied/error because the service-linked role does not yet exist. No attribute of the domain references the role, and no `depends_on` expresses this ordering, so the dependency is missing.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch is deployed inside a VPC (it references module.aws_vpc and aws_security_group.opensearch_access), but it has no dependency on aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch. AWS requires the AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService service-linked role to exist before a domain with vpc_options can be created; on the first apply (or whenever var.create_iam_service_linked_role is true and the role is being created in the same run) the domain creation will fail because no dependency orders the role ahead of the domain. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch] to the domain resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The VPC-based OpenSearch/Elasticsearch domain (":resource.aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch") uses vpc_options, which requires the AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService service-linked role to exist before the domain can be created. The project declares ":resource.aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch" (gated by var.create_iam_service_linked_role) for exactly this purpose, but the domain has no dependency on it — neither an attribute reference nor an explicit depends_on. If var.create_iam_service_linked_role is true, both resources will be created in parallel and the domain creation can fail with a "no service-linked role" API error on first apply. The provider documentation explicitly requires depends_on for this case (service-linked roles cannot be referenced via a data dependency), so a bare depends_on is the correct fix.
